note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
Kings tells the same account in its own way. It had already said Manasseh “hath done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, which were before him, and hath made Judah also to sin with his idols.” He went above the Amorites; Manasseh was a monster. Chronicles gives more of the detail: he “caused his children to pass through the fire”, ancient abortions, burning his babies alive; he observed times, used enchantments and witchcraft, dealt with a familiar spirit and with wizards; he was a sorcerer. And he put an idol in the temple.

Then Kings adds what Chronicles leaves out: “Moreover Manasseh shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another.” Babies on babies. That is a lot of blood, from one end of Jerusalem to the other. And it was not only him: the people did the same thing, for this was “beside his sin wherewith he made Judah to sin, in doing that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

Manasseh was behind a lot of death, sorcery and witchcraft; he did evil way beyond worthy of death. He killed babies, he went into witchcraft, he defiled the temple. And yet, when he was in affliction and humbled himself greatly, the Lord forgave Manasseh, heard his supplication, and put him back on the throne. The Lord has mercy on whom he will have mercy.

That is why it is so important for us to learn humility. People fall, and the Most High is able to raise them up again, like David. But don't abuse it. All of us in here ain't David; don't think, I can do what David did. No, negro, you ain't David. You're not Manasseh. You ain't Moses. The Lord puts it there to remind us that the graces and mercies of Christ were around back then too, from time to time. Don't get stupid and get prideful. Humility.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God, and the words of the seers that spake to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel.” That is another book, the book of the kings of Israel.

We do have the prayer of Manasseh; it is in the Apocrypha. But that prayer is also part of the book of the kings of Israel, and that book we don't have.

So what are we to do with the books we don't have? Christ answers it in Revelation: “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come.” Today we have 80 books. Don't go looking for other books, and don't try to mix in something someone just found, like a book called Lilith, Adam's second wife. Leave all those books alone.

Read on: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”. If you overcome your lust, the temptations and the white man's lies, and hold on to that little faith and that little understanding you got from these 80 books, you will rule the nations. What is in these 80 books, the laws and the prophecies of what is going to take place, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
“His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, and all his sin, and his trespass, and the places wherein he built high places, and set up groves and graven images, before he was humbled: behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.” So there is a book called the sayings of the seers, the same name as Captain Horab's show, and we don't have it today.

The Lord took those books away. Why? Because some things in them we are not to understand today. He wants us to just trust in him. Some of the things he did back then, he does not want us to have in these last days. And some books were taken away so that the white man could come and lie on the earth and spread all these lies, because some things in those other books were too plain for us to understand. Even though the Vatican took those books and hid them, the Lord allowed that.

One of those missing books is the heart of this class: “Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord”. The Lord there is Christ. He is not only going to war in the future; he has been warring since the beginning. We don't have that book, but we can go into the scriptures and see its record in parts, as here in Joshua 10, where the sun stood still until Israel had avenged themselves upon their enemies.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh “caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom”. That valley, Gehenna, was where Israel burned its garbage, our refuse; the Muslims call it Gehenna, their hell. Where garbage used to be burned, they burned their children, in honor of Baal.

There was an order to it. In the spring they held orgies in honor of Ashtoreth, the fertility goddess, a black Hamite deity whose star is Venus and whose nose is knocked off the statues. Everyone slept with everyone, and the women got pregnant. Nine months later, in the winter, came the bull god, Baal, the sun god the Egyptians called Apis. The babies were laid on the plates of the brass bull with a fire under it and around it; as they burned they wiggled off into the flame, and drums were beaten to drown out their screams. That is what Manasseh was doing, by the thousands. Carnival babies, Freaknik and the club today are the same worship of that goddess.

Why sacrifice the babies? Ashtoreth gave birth to a baby god, Tammuz, and Tammuz died as an infant. The same way she lost her child, the women had to lose theirs, and the same way she wept for her child, they had to weep for the children they sacrificed on the altar. That is why Jesus is always pictured as a baby with Mary.

Ezekiel saw it: “Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the Lord’s house which was toward the north; and, behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.” That is what they had to do once they were in that idolatry: weep for the babies they themselves had sacrificed. And it was worse than what is brought out here.

precepts.point: Manasseh made Judah err and do worse than the heathen the Lord had destroyed before them, the nations Joshua and the elders were sent to kill out of the land for the very same works.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
“So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.” Worse than the nations we were killing out of the land for doing the exact same thing. What does that mean? Wisdom of Solomon gives an idea.

“For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of thy holy land”. Our fathers were Joshua, Caleb and the elders who succeeded Moses; when we entered the promised land we had to war with the nations already there. The old inhabitants were the Canaanites, the Hamites living in the land before we got there.

“Whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices”: odious works are filth, evil, vile things, and that is what Manasseh was doing. “And also those merciless murderers of children”: Manasseh did it and had the people do it. “and devourers of man’s flesh, and the feasts of blood”: cannibalism, drinking blood, eating flesh. Who knows what Manasseh was doing, but he was worse than the heathen, so we have to factor this in. “and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help”: we were killing our own kids.

“That the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God’s children.” The Lord had us go in and kill those nations out of the land because they were doing these things. Then we got the land, turned around, and did the exact same thing and worse under Manasseh, as Ahab did in his time. Manasseh was one of the worst kings Judah ever had.

precepts.text: The captains of the king of Assyria take Manasseh among the thorns and carry him bound to Babylon, then held by Assyria.
precepts.point: The history shows a power struggle beginning, where Assyrian kings ruled over Babylon, and later Babylonian kings ruled over Assyria; Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the Lord brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.”

The rest of the acts of Manasseh are written in the chronicles, and this is part of what Kings leaves out. The captains of the king of Assyria carried him bound to Babylon, which was then a province under Assyria. There he repented and prayed, and the prayer of Manasseh is recorded in the Apocrypha, prayed while he was held captive in Babylon.

It also shows the power struggle beginning, with Assyrian kings ruling over Babylon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer. For all that do these things are an abomination unto the Lord”. And: “Thou shalt be perfect with the Lord thy God.”

Manasseh did every one of them: “he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards”. Every one of these things is a commandment he broke. Passing children through the fire is child sacrifice, the same spirit as abortion today.

The law says “because of these abominations the Lord thy God doth drive them out from before thee.” Manasseh brought those same abominations into the house of the Lord: he “built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord”, and “wrought much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.”

precepts.text: Doing worse than the heathen is the same rebuke Paul gives, fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles found among the people.
precepts.point: He sets a carved idol in the house of God, the very house of which the Most High said to David and Solomon, In this house and in Jerusalem will I put my name for ever, and Manasseh makes Judah do worse than the heathen the Lord destroyed before them.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.” Doing worse than the heathen is the same rebuke Paul gives: a sin found among the people that is not so much as named among the Gentiles.

That is Manasseh. He set “a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God”, the very house of which God said to David and Solomon, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen before all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name for ever”. “So Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel.”

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
The curse said: “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.”

That came upon Manasseh. “And the Lord spake to Manasseh, and to his people: but they would not hearken.” So the Lord “brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.” The kings of Israel that were once kings were brought down into captivity, exactly as the curses warned.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“And for our sins and our fathers’ we with our brethren and our kings and our priests were given up unto the kings of the earth, to the sword, and to captivity, and for a prey with shame, unto this day.”

The kings were not spared. Manasseh, king in Jerusalem, was taken “among the thorns”, bound “with fetters”, and carried “to Babylon”, because he and his people “would not hearken.” For their sins and their fathers’ sins, the kings of Israel were given up into the hands of the kings of the earth.

precepts.text: The graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and not desired, for they are an abomination to the Most High, the example Manasseh follows in casting down the idols.
precepts.point: He repairs the altar of the Lord, sacrifices peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and commands Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel, though the people still sacrifice in the high places, only unto the Lord their God.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” The graven images of the nations were to be destroyed and not desired, for they are an abomination to the Most High.

That is the example Manasseh followed once he was humbled. “And he took away the strange gods, and the idol out of the house of the Lord, and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the house of the Lord, and in Jerusalem, and cast them out of the city.” He kept none of it.

Then “he repaired the altar of the Lord, and sacrificed thereon peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.” He also built the wall of the city of David and “put captains of war in all the fenced cities of Judah.” The people still sacrificed in the high places, “yet unto the Lord their God only.”

precepts.text: The prayer of Manasseh king of Judah, found before the books of Maccabees, is his cry to the God of his fathers when he was held in Babylon.
precepts.point: This is the prayer of Manasseh, a writing of the Apocrypha found before the Maccabees, which is part of the Bible. Manasseh sleeps with his fathers and Amon his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“O Lord, Almighty God of our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their righteous seed”. This is the prayer of Manasseh king of Judah, his cry to the God of his fathers when he was held in Babylon.

Chronicles points right to it: “the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer unto his God”, and “His prayer also, and how God was intreated of him, and all his sin, and his trespass”, “behold, they are written among the sayings of the seers.” That prayer is a writing of the Apocrypha, found before the books of Maccabees, and it is part of the Bible.

God was intreated of him, and the wicked king was humbled. “So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house: and Amon his son reigned in his stead.”

precepts.text: A humble man asks the Most High to scourge his thoughts and discipline his heart when he errs, so his ignorance does not increase and his sins abound to his destruction.
precepts.point: The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them. Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins”. A humble man asks the Most High to scourge his thoughts and discipline his heart when he errs, so his ignorance does not increase and his sins do not abound to his destruction.

Amon never asked. He “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as did Manasseh his father”, sacrificing “unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made”, “And humbled not himself before the Lord, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.”

His sins abounded to his own destruction: “his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.” The people of the land slew the conspirators “and made Josiah his son king in his stead.”

precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of men is fully set in them to do evil, which is why Amon's evil increased.
precepts.point: The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.”

That is why Amon’s evil increased. He saw his father’s idols stand and took up serving them, and with no sentence executed speedily his heart was fully set to do evil: he “humbled not himself before the Lord”, “but Amon trespassed more and more.” He reigned only “two years in Jerusalem” before “his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.”

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: Amon is twenty two years old when he begins to reign and reigns two years in Jerusalem, doing evil in the sight of the Lord as Manasseh his father, sacrificing to all the carved images Manasseh had made.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: But Amon does not humble himself before the Lord as his father had humbled himself; instead he trespasses more and more, and his own servants conspire against him and slay him in his house.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction.
